title: Tenant-context middleware (X-Tenant-Id enforcement) and audit writer service
objective: Port the tenant middleware and the audit writer: server-side verification of X-Tenant-Id against caller memberships or Internal cross-tenant grant on every tenant-scoped route, explicit tenant parameter threaded to the data layer, and a shared audit_log writer used by all privileged/business operations (M-05, M-06, N-01, P-13, spec 13).
scope: lib/tenancy: Hono middleware tenantContext() — requires X-Tenant-Id on tenant-scoped routes, verifies membership via user_tenants or Internal/global cross-tenant permission, rejects with 403 (no leakage); attaches TenantContext { tenantId, isCrossTenantAccess } to request context; removed (soft-deleted) tenants rejected for normal workflows
Route classification convention: tenant-scoped vs cross-tenant/global routes (Tenant Manager, global template, /me) — explicit registration, never inferred

domains/audit: writeAudit(db|trx, entry) service writing audit_log rows (actor, tenant where applicable, action, entity type/id, jsonb before/after, correlation id, timestamp); participates in the caller's transaction
Cross-tenant access by Internal users is itself audited (spec 13)
404-for-cross-tenant-IDs convention helper: repository misses and cross-tenant hits are indistinguishable (N-01)
out_of_scope: RLS SET LOCAL wiring (T-014 — builds on TenantContext)
Audit read/inspection endpoints (only if present in the reference API — not in the section 12 inventory)
implementation_details: Middleware order: authenticate() -> tenantContext() -> requirePermission(); requirePermission resolves the effective set for the verified tenant.
TenantContext carried via typed Hono variables; the data layer's tenant helpers take tenantId explicitly from it — no ambient globals (spec 13).

Audit writer accepts an optional transaction handle so audit rows commit atomically with the business change (port of the .NET pattern); jsonb payload shape matches the reference (before/after field naming).
Never trust client-supplied tenant/user/role ids beyond the verified context; header value validated as bigint.
Internal cross-tenant grant path: users with the explicit cross-tenant permission may set X-Tenant-Id to any active tenant; the audit row records isCrossTenantAccess.

unit: Header parsing/validation edge cases (missing, non-numeric, negative) -> 400/403 per reference semantics
integration: Member of tenant A with X-Tenant-Id A passes; X-Tenant-Id B (non-member) -> 403 with no information leakage
Internal user with cross-tenant grant accesses tenant B; audit row records the cross-tenant access
Removed tenant rejected for normal callers
Audit writer inside a rolled-back transaction leaves no audit row (atomicity)
e2e: Tenant isolation and cross-tenant Internal-mode specs adapted in T-043

history.message: Task generated by Planner from approved spec.md. Maps to M-05, M-06, N-01, P-13, spec 13 tenant context.
Delegated to Implementor. T-013 and T-031 run in parallel (lib/tenancy + domains/audit vs src/server/jobs + api/queue + api/cron + a jobs migration). Orchestrator owns harness JSON.

Tenant-context middleware + audit writer implemented; T-009's tenant slot filled without reordering the pipeline. .NET semantics MEASURED: malformed/missing X-Tenant-Id -> 403 not 400 (TenantContextMiddleware.cs:50-55 folds both into WriteForbiddenAsync :120-132); check order exists -> active -> user_tenants -> global grant -> deny (TenantAccessValidator.cs:26-61); cross-tenant grant resolves in the GLOBAL scope (:55, tenantId null); exempt prefixes /tenants /global /me /intake (:20-26) with prefix-BOUNDARY matching (:102-110) so /api/v1/tenantsummary is not exempted. TWO DELIBERATE DEVIATIONS FOR EVALUATOR RULING: (1) uniform denial message - the reference returns reason-specific details (DescribeDenial :112-118: 'Tenant does not exist.' vs 'Tenant is not active.' vs 'Caller is not a member.'), which is an EXISTENCE ORACLE contradicting AC-020 and spec 384; collapsed to one constant, status still 403, reason logged server-side only. (2) audit details casing - the reference emits PascalCase Before/After (AuditWriter.cs:33 has no naming policy; pinned by BusinessAssignmentEndpointsTests.cs:135-136) but T-003's migration documents lowercase and the reference was itself inconsistent (AuditWriterTests.cs:29,41 uses lowercase); chose lowercase to match the in-repo contract every later task builds on - `details` appears in no frontend contract. UNDECLARED ROUTES FAIL CLOSED: an unclassified /api/v1 route is tenant-scoped and 403s without a verified header; only the explicit GLOBAL_ROUTE_PREFIXES list is exempt (mutating the default to global turned 28 tests red). N-01 achieved BY CONSTRUCTION: lookups go through forTenant(), so a cross-tenant row arrives as undefined - identical to nonexistent; requireFound has no branch that could distinguish them; proven by deep-equality across five denial reasons plus an exact body-key-set assertion. 13 mutants all red; positive controls both ways (deny-everything failed 7, allow-everything failed 10), so the suite cannot be satisfied by blanket allow OR deny. TWO MUTANTS INITIALLY SURVIVED AND WERE FIXED: (a) resolving the cross-tenant grant in the REQUESTED tenant's scope passed everything because the test granted in tenant A and requested B - non-discriminating; a test granting view_any_tenant INSIDE tenant B was added, and this is the ESCALATION case: without it any tenant admin able to grant permissions in their own tenant could mint cross-tenant access; (b) assertAudited's 'exactly one row' strictness was itself untested - now fed duplicates, important because every downstream domain proves audit coverage through that helper. Implementor also found and fixed a fragility in its own test: substring-matching tenant ids against the body false-reds when a reset lowers ids ('1' matches 'rfc9110') and passes vacuously otherwise; replaced with exact key-set assertions. SCOPE CALL FLAGGED: implementor wired the production composition roots - neither passed `tenancy`, so the tenant slot was EMPTY in production; silent today (no tenant-scoped routes exist yet) but a cross-tenant hole the moment one lands. Added defaultTenancyDeps() and pinned it in auth-wiring.test.ts. Gates: typecheck 0, lint 0, npm test 51 files / 805 tests 0 skipped, ci:test 0.

Evaluator: PASS. Gates re-run independently: npm test 51 files / 805 tests / 0 skipped exit 0; ci:test exit 0 (805 floor); typecheck 0; lint 0; db:validate 0. Three mutants reproduced first-hand and all killed: (1) THE ESCALATION MUTANT - resolving the cross-tenant grant in the REQUESTED tenant's scope (access.ts tenantId:null -> tenantId) is killed by exactly 'does not honour a view_any_tenant grant scoped to the REQUESTED tenant' (1 failed / 29 passed), confirming the guard against a tenant admin minting cross-tenant access is pinned by a discriminating test; (2) reintroducing the reference's reason-specific denial strings is killed by 'answers every denial reason with a byte-identical body'; (3) flipping the fail-closed classification default to 'global' turns 29 tests red. RULING 1 (uniform denial): deviation from the reference is CORRECT. DescribeDenial (TenantContextMiddleware.cs:112-118) is an existence oracle letting any authenticated caller enumerate which tenants exist and which are soft-deleted; a faithful port would preserve a security defect contradicting AC-020, N-01 and spec line 384 ('403 permission/tenant violation (no leakage)'). Collapse verified complete: single ForbiddenError construction site with one constant message; all five denial reasons deep-equal in body with exact key-set {detail,status,title,type} pinned; status uniformly 403 including malformed/missing header (measured reference semantics); headers identical by construction (one problem+json render path; correlationId fixed-length). Only residual discriminator found: response TIMING differs marginally by reason (1 DB query for tenant_not_found vs 3 for not_member) - theoretical, unmeasured, also present (worse, explicit) in the reference; recorded as a note, not a finding. RULING 2 (details casing): lowercase before/after is CORRECT for the target system. The reference had NO single contract - AuditWriter.cs:33 serializes caller anonymous objects with no naming policy, so casing was per-call-site: PascalCase in BusinessAssignmentEndpointsTests.cs:135-136, lowercase in AuditWriterTests.cs:29,41. Verified `details` appears in NO consumer contract: QuoteIQ.Api/Endpoints has no audit read endpoint, and src/ui contains zero references to audit details payloads. T-003's migration comment (20260718001300_audit_log.sql:18-22) documents lowercase and assertAudited enforces key totality; standardizing on lowercase now, before any audit rows exist, is the cheap correct move. Also verified: production composition roots (api/v1/[[...segments]].ts:29, scripts/dev/serve-api.ts:64) pass tenancy via defaultTenancyDeps() and auth-wiring.test.ts pins both plus the middleware order authenticate(171) -> tenantContext(182) -> permissionResolution(190) in router/app.ts; audit writer transaction participation proven both ways (rollback leaves no row; root-handle escape documented and pinned); assertAudited enforces exactly-one plus both keys and its strictness is itself tested with duplicates; undeclared /api/v1 routes fail closed; unknown routes 404 not 403; verified tenant id (not header text) reaches SQL. AC-021 discharged at the helper/convention level only - the per-endpoint 404 sweep is T-024..T-027's obligation per the known-limits ruling; e2e adaptation remains T-043.
